CBDB-Desktop: Association Pairs, Associations and Browser label revisions, second pass, 2026-10-27

The first pass on these three forms (2026-10-26) used an older 330-row copy of the MS Access FormLabels table. This second pass checks them against the **updated 643-row table** from the user's current CBDB database, which adds rows for all three (LAAP 16–35, LAA 12–36, BIO 54–58, BROWSE 4–7, SAN 9, SF_KIN 8–11, SF_BID, SF_BSD) and corrects some of the rows the first pass had flagged. It also applies the decisions of 2026-10-27: the regional-usage rule, the Store / Recall / Import wording, and a translated Navigation link (see the conventions document). Changes are in the three forms' index.html files only. Each page was loaded in a scripted browser (jsdom) and every changed label checked in all three languages, with no script errors. **Not yet tested in the running app.** Copies of the files before this pass were kept as assoc_pairs.before-second-pass.html, associations.before-second-pass.html and browser.before-second-pass.html.

How to revert a label

As in the first-pass reports: change the value of the key in the translation object (T on Association Pairs, translations on Associations and Browser), in the language concerned. Each changed line has a comment naming its FormLabels row and the earlier wording. Where the English changed, the same text was also changed in the HTML element; setLanguage overwrites it on load.

Notes

**LBL-51.** "Import List of People" and "Clear List of People" are longer than before, and the Person List section has three buttons in one row. **Check whether the row wraps.** 刪除人名 ("delete names") is the table's wording; the button clears the imported list and does not delete anything from the database.

**LBL-52.** Store Person IDs follows the table (LAAP 21, 存儲人物代碼), with 儲存 in traditional under the regional-usage rule.

**AP-1.** setLanguage wrote Run Query as plain text (t.runQuery), so the ▶ shown in the HTML disappeared as soon as the page loaded. Every other form writes '▶ ' + t.runQuery, and this one now does the same.

**Not changed.** Save to UCINet stays 保存于UCINet. LAAP 24 has 保存為 UCINet 格式 ("save in UCINet format"), unlike every other Save row in the table (LAAP 26 Gephi, 35 Neo4j, LAA 23 UCINet are all 保存于…), so it looks like an outlier to correct in the table.

Notes

**LBL-56.** Settles the open "Sub-units" wording. **Check the address row:** Include Subordinate Units, Use XY References and the All Places button now share one row, and all three are longer than before.

**LBL-57.** The address and dynasty clear buttons both read "All" through one all key. They now have their own keys, taken from LAA 15 and 29. The all key is still used for "All" next to Select Dynasties when no dynasty is chosen.

**LBL-60.** This form's link said "← Home" where the other forms say "← Navigation". It now says Navigation and is translated. It also got id="lnkNavigation".

**LBL-61.** The association and address pickers open from "…" buttons with no text (Issue 1 of the first-pass report). The buttons got ids (btnPickAssoc, btnPickAddr) and, through setLanguage, tooltips from LAA 4 and 13. The layout is unchanged.

# Questions from the first pass, now answered by the table.

- Rows 54–58 of BrowserLabelTranslations.xlsx are in the updated table as BIO 54–58, so no rows need adding.
- BIO 54 has 社交機構. The Browser keeps 社會機構 by the user's decision, so the table row should be changed.

Rows not used, and one question

- **BROWSE 5 (Clear Search 清除查詢結果) and 6 (Search by Surname + Office 查詢姓+官名):** the Browser has no such controls.
- **BROWSE 7, Save to File 保存於檔案 / 保存于档案.** This is probably the Access counterpart of **Export Profile**, but I wasn't sure enough to rename the button. If it is the counterpart, there are two options:
   - **Rename the button:** "Save to File", with 保存于檔案 in traditional and 保存于文件 in simplified. In the mainland, 档案 means "archives", so 文件 is the mainland term for a computer file.
   - **Keep the wording:** "Export Profile" (匯出人物資料 / 导出人物资料), which says more about what is saved.
